# Independent source review of cohort A freshness

Reviewed frozen `28f189d7eb84131569c903a0e6bdb9663cf5e6f5` (initial harness `9f3390dcc5c04984d1371905b86ca63d1fe26b96`, application scheduling checkpoint `8367e0a1`) against common source `773f7746466caf0ba4eff70a741e9594d07f39cc`. Candidate budget SHA256 is `f559ddeab71671daeccc0a39ad31ed347680835abe1da90f8414ecfda7dbfb30`. Source-only review; no application files, engines, builds, tests or large fixture hashes were changed/run by the reviewer.

No blocker was found to the isolated candidate screen. Read contract 2 remains explicitly different from the v1 submitted-write barrier and ineligible for full promotion.

`benchmark-read-scheduling.mjs:21–40` records real patch submissions and returned receipts, checks consecutive FIFO ACK positions and maintains pending commands independently of queried clocks. A read snapshots this ledger synchronously at invocation (`:47–50`). Latest reads must return at least the ACK position already observed then; explicit historical cuts instead require exact K (`:60–73`). An older coherent read may legitimately trail ACKs delivered while it runs; return-time lag and commit visibility ahead of the ACK callback are recorded separately. No engine commit timestamp is inferred.

Summaries select only `phase==='measured'` (`:79–97`), excluding first/warmup/final verification. The measured latency timer starts before observer invocation and the real public call (`benchmark-scale.mjs:127–142`), so invocation instrumentation, queue waits and decoding remain included. Completion diagnostics and the typed oracle run after the stopped sample, as declared; measured wall/CPU still includes that work. Final verification remains outside measured phase wall/CPU. Actual native-port control-scope IDs (`benchmark-read-scheduling.mjs:102–118`) are distinct from logical client IDs and are not native-task concurrency evidence.

Reusable runners keep the original query, typed correction oracle and read/write loops when hooks are absent (`benchmark-antijoin-cost.mjs:184–202`; `benchmark-scale.mjs:134–146`). Budget validation preserves the original numerical limits and control fingerprints, allowing only the declared application artifact difference (`benchmark-read-scheduling.mjs:127–139`). The small-screen follow-up retains runtime/harness/source pins while explicitly omitting numerical qualification (`:145–171`; `benchmark-antijoin-cost.mjs:294–295`).

Two nonblocking coverage improvements were sent to the author: a pure first/warmup/measured/final filtering case (the five current pure fixtures all use measured phase), and an explicit distinct physical-port-count assertion in `afterCell`. The current runner already requires all sixteen native leases to be observed, and the hook records actual port IDs. Runtime qualification and any promising fresh/reverse comparison remain separate from this source review.
